summary: Taisei Iwata is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a lecturer at Rissho University (attested 1984), a professor at Otani University (attested 1996), and an advisor at Minobusan University (attested 2026).
Taisen Deshimaru was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Kodo Sawaki from around 1936 to 1965. He founded the Association Zen Internationale and La Gendronnière.

Taishu Tagami, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, studied at Komazawa University and earned a master's at the University of Tokyo (~1959–1964). He served as a professor at Komazawa University (~1978–2005) and concurrent lecturer at Eastern Institute (attested 1990).

Taishun Mibu was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Taisho University from around 1933 to 1937. He later served as library director at Taisho University from around 1952 to 1980.

Taitetsu Unno studied English literature at UC Berkeley (~1947–1951) and Buddhist studies at the University of Tokyo (~1951–1968, M.A., Ph.D.). A scholar of Buddhism, religion, and philosophy, he was Jill Ker Conway Professor Emeritus of Religion at Smith College (1971–1998).

Taitsu Kono, a Buddhist studies scholar, studied at Hanazono University (~1950–1954) and under traditional teacher Mumon Yamada (~1954–1988). He later held a post at Hanazono University from around 1993 to 2000.

Taixu was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied under Jing'an, Jichan, and Renshan Yang, and at Jinling Scriptural Press. He led Minnan Buddhist Institute (1927) and founded institutions including Wuchang Buddhist Institute, Tianning Buddhist College, and World Fellowship of Buddhists.

Taizan Maezumi studied at Komazawa University, Soji-ji, SFSU, and under Hakujun Kuroda, Hakuun Ryoko Yasutani, and Koryu Osaka. He served as priest at Zenshuji Soto Mission (1956) and founded the Zen Center of Los Angeles, Kuroda Institute, and White Plum Asanga.
Tak Pui Sze is a scholar in sinology and religious studies who completed a PhD at the University of British Columbia under the doctoral supervision of Jinhua Chen (attested 2012).

Taka Yanagisawa was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Japan Women's University. She served as Director of the Department of Fine Arts at the Tokyo National Research Institute for Cultural Properties from around 1988 to 1992.
Takahiko Kameyama is a Buddhist studies scholar who has held posts as a professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies and as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University (both attested 2015).
Takahiko Sato is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at Koyasan University, with posts attested in 2015 and 2026.

Takahiro Asano studied at Chiba, Doshisha, Washington, and York universities (PhD 2015). Active in religious and Buddhist studies, he worked at Kyoto International Social Welfare Exchange Centre (2000–2008) and held associate professorships at Japan Lutheran College (2021–2026) and Musashino University (2026).

Takahiro Kato is an Indology and philosophy scholar with a Dr.Phil from Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg. As of 2026, he is attested as a professor at the University of Tokyo and affiliated with the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.
Takako Abe is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who served as a lecturer (attested 2013–2017) and faculty member (attested 2026) at Taisho University.

Takamaro Shigaraki, a Buddhist studies scholar, earned a PhD at Ryukoku University and studied at UH Mānoa and the Institute of Buddhist Studies. At Ryukoku University, he was professor (1970) and President (1989–1995), later chairing Bukkyo Dendo Kyokai (1995–2008).

Takamatsu Yoshie studied at Tōkyō Senmon Gakkō, Waseda University (Doctor of Letters, 1931), and the University of Paris. He founded Waseda University, taught English at its high school (1906), and served as a Waseda lecturer (1908, 1910) and Dean of Literature (1930).

Takami Inoue is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. Inoue was a doctoral candidate at the University of California, Santa Barbara (attested 2003) and served as Professor of Shin Buddhist Studies at Otani University.

Takamichi Fukita, a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar, studied at Taisho and Bukkyo universities under Zenno Ishigami, Shozen Kumoi, and Yuichi Kajiyama, with postdoctoral mentoring from Heinz Bechert. He served as a lecturer and faculty member at Bukkyo University (attested 1999, 2013).

Takanobu Takahashi studied at the University of Tokyo, Madurai Kamaraj University under Tamilannal, and Utrecht University (PhD). A scholar of Indology and linguistics, he was associate professor at Shitennoji University (1991) and the University of Tokyo (1996, 1999–2016).
